newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss Re sets up ART division.
newsitem.headline: Swiss Re sets up ART division.

text.p: Swiss Reinsurance Co said it was creating a new division, Swiss Re New Markets, dedicated to the fast-growing area of alternative risk transfer markets.
A Swiss Re statement said certain joint ventures in related business, including one with Credit Suisse Group and Winterthur Insurance, would remain outside the new division.

The reorganisation upgraded the standing of the business within the the group and was aimed at bundling the group's expertise across product lines to better serve customers, a Swiss Re spokesman said.
"Swiss Re New Markets incorporates the business units of the former Swiss Re ART Division, including Credit & Surety and Aviation," the statement said.

"Certain joint ventures -- International Risk Management Group (IRMG), Securitas Capital LLC and Reinsurance Finance Consultants -- will retain their separate identities while operating within the new functional organisation," it said.
Reinsurance Finance Consultants is a joint venture with Credit Suisse Group and Winterthur.
For insurers, Swiss RE said its new divisions would offer capital market techniques in addition to traditional reinsurance solutions.
For corporate clients, Swiss Re said it would offer "a holistic approach to risk management" including captive management, structured financial arrangements and significant risk capacity.
The new division will start operating on July 1 in Zurich, New York and London.
Analysts welcomed the move as a step to strengthing Swiss Re's activities in ART since chief executive Walter Kielholz first set up the existing division in 1995.
Heinrich-Horst Wiemer of Credit Suisse First Boston equity research said that while the new status alone did not create added value, it shows how important ART is to Swiss Re.
"It is important. It is a growth market," he said.

Swiss Re's existing ART division took in premiums of around two billion Swiss francs in 1996, analysts estimate. That compares with total group premiums of 12.8 billion Swiss francs in 1995, the last reported year.
"It also makes it possible for a third party to take a stake in the new unit," Wiemer said.
But he quickly added that Swiss Re New Markets could very well folow other avenues of cooperation with banks and insurers and did not need to offer an equity stake.
Swiss Re spoeksman Otto Kern also dismissed speculation on the Swiss stock exchange that the company could offer a stake in the new division to bank group Credit Suisse.
"We have no such plans at the moment," Kern told Reuters. -- Zurich Newsroom, +41-1-631 7340
